title: Eval parity loss traced to sampling config change + prefix-merging optimization in private/dedicated pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer (enterprise health analytics vendor) reported nondeterministic failures in their automated eval suite after last-week runtime change. Failures are limited to Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) pools and manifest as: extra tokens appended to outputs, truncated JSON responses, and missing stop-sequence detection on otherwise-identical prompts. Customer evals regressed within hours of a config roll that changed global sampling defaults and enabled prefix-merging optimization for private routing. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and long-term fixes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use customer's canonical eval prompt set (attached manifest) against model: redwood/open-7b-v2 in a Private tenant using dedicated pool config
2) Run eval harness with runtime default sampling config (sampling_policy_v2) and with prefix-merging enabled in routing layer
3) Observe generated outputs: several cases show stop tokens not recognized leading to runaway generation or JSON truncation at different offsets
4) Re-run with sampling defaults explicitly set to historical values (sampling_policy_v1) OR with prefix-merging disabled; parity is restored for majority of failing cases.
root_cause_summary: Two coincident changes exposed an interaction bug in private/dedicated routing: (A) the global sampling default switch (sampling_policy_v2) changes token selection fallbacks and introduces a subtle whitespace-sensitive post-processing step; (B) the prefix-merging optimization in the routing layer concatenates cached prefixes with incoming prompts and performs an aggressive trim that can remove sentinel/stop-markers when combined with quantized kernel whitespace normalization in the serving runtime. Alone, neither change caused customer-visible failures — together they altered token alignment for stop-sequence matching in ~0.7% of requests for this customer's prompt shapes.
mitigation_actions: - Emergency rollback: reverted global sampling default for affected tenants to sampling_policy_v1 (rolled 2025-02-11 02:10 UTC).
- Temporary configuration: disabled prefix-merging optimization for Private/Dedicated routing until patch is deployed (feature flag off).
- Patch in progress: routing change to preserve explicit sentinel tokens and avoid whitespace-trimming around cached prefix boundaries (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1837).
- Added guarded stop-token canonicalization in serving runtime that matches previous behavior for quantized kernels (under review).
- Customer communication: dispatched incident summary and ETA to SRE/AM teams; scheduled weekly checkpoints with customer until release.
followups: - Add e2e regression test that runs customer prompt sets under both sampling_policy_v1 and sampling_policy_v2 in CI (owner: Marco Li).
- Expand eval harness to include stop-token edge cases + whitespace normalization tests (owner: QA Team).
- Postmortem due 2025-03-01 with root-cause timeline and action items for cross-team guardrails (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Consider a canary policy for sampling defaults that excludes Dedicated/Private for 2 weeks before org-wide toggle (product discussion).
